DRIVER STATION

Take the field.

WASD moves relative to the camera. Left / Right arrows turn; Q / E also work. Tank uses W/S to move and A/D or arrows to turn.

Space shoots into your hub inside your alliance zone. Outside it, Space passes to the marked home-zone landing target. Hold Left Shift to run the intake. P pauses; R resets to robot selection. Scroll to zoom; drag in Free orbit to orbit.

Controller (standard mapping): left stick drives, right stick turns, A / Cross or right trigger shoots and passes, hold left trigger to run the intake, the D-pad selects a robot, A / Cross starts the match and returns to selection afterward, and Start / Options starts or pauses the match. Connect the controller, click the game, then press a button. Standard-mapped controllers work best; other controllers with two sticks use a generic mapping.

The translucent extension marks the intake side; the small housing marks the shooter. Robots that fit start at a trench; taller robots start by a bump.

Before a match, choose a pre-loaded team. A three-second countdown runs before AUTO starts; pause or reset it at any time. To choose another, use Choose robot to reset the match.

All dumpers lock chassis aiming while shooting; release shoot to turn manually.

Team 316 cannot intake while shooting or passing on the move. Team 5895 uses two swiveling corner turrets with a shared feed rate.

Turret: swivels and shoots on the move. Big dumper: can shoot while moving. PID-style aim assist turns the chassis or turret toward the target; moving accuracy controls spread. Lanes fire slightly irregular streams, sharing the average feed rate (up to 25 fuel/s). Drive speed is limited to 30% while shooting or passing with fuel. Shots outside the configured scoring range fall short. Longer shots use a higher arc. The yellow fill rises with stored fuel.

AUTO is driver-controlled in this simulator, as requested. Timing follows the 2026 sequence: 20s AUTO, 3s scoring delay, 10s transition, four alternating 25s hub shifts, and 30s end game. AUTO's fuel winner is inactive first; ties are randomized. Both hubs are active in AUTO, transition and end game. A 3s scoring grace follows deactivation.

All hub entries return to center, including inactive ones. One robot starts with 8 fuel; the center has 400, depots 48, and outposts 48 stored. Total: 504.

2v2: Create a 2v2 room for one player and one AI teammate on each alliance. Both bots use team 2539 and play each other.

Private rooms: Create a 1v1 room (blue vs red) or co-op room (both blue), share its code, choose robots and ready up. Both drivers control AUTO. P pauses for everyone; Leave room ends the shared match. Disconnects pause the match and reserve your seat for 30 seconds. Reconnected players press Resume. The room creator runs the match and should keep the game tab open. Hiding the host tab pauses the match; either player can resume when the host returns.

Single player or private two-player matches. No climbing or human-player feeding. Foul assessment covers AUTO center crossing, robot contact after crossing, and direct tower-protection contact; referee-judgment fouls and fuel-mediated tower contact are not modeled. Field motion and distribution are simplified; unspecified team settings are estimates.
